title: Activities by type
summary: The same activities as the input list, grouped by their type: analysis, development, meeting, whatever the activity types table holds.
text:
Activities by type

The same activities as the input list, grouped by their type: analysis,
development, meeting, whatever the activity types table holds.

It answers the question the flat list answers badly - where is the time going? - without
counting anything: the rows are simply gathered under the type they belong to, and the groups can
be opened and closed.

For the same question answered with numbers instead of rows, see the dashboard and
its pie chart by type.

title: Activity calendar
summary: The activities on a calendar, by their date. It answers what is happening this week?, which is the one question a list of rows answers badly.
text:
Activity calendar

The activities on a calendar, by their date. It answers what is happening this week?, which is
the one question a list of rows answers badly.

It is the same activities as everywhere else: what changes is that the day, not the row, is the
unit. Open one to see it in full.

title: Activity input
summary: The list of activities, and the form to record one without passing through the wizard.
keywords: What an activity is made of
text:
Activity input

The list of activities, and the form to record one without passing through the wizard.

 What an activity is made of

 Field | |
 
 Description | What was done. Required. |
 Phase | The phase of the project. Required: it carries the project, and the project carries the customer. |
 Employee | Who did it. Required. |
 Role | In which role. Required. |
 Type | What kind of work. Required. |
 Activity Date | The day. Required. |
 Start Time, End Time | The hours of the day it took. |
 Status | Where it stands. |
 Duration | The hours, worked out from the times. |

 Finding what you recorded

The Search panel above the list is how you come back to an activity: by date, by employee, by
customer, by what the description says. The toolbar offers Download in TXT and Download in
CSV for what the list is showing.

 The same activities, elsewhere

The same rows are grouped by type, laid out as a
report, put on a calendar and counted in the
dashboard. Nothing of that is a copy: it is one table, seen five ways.

title: Activity report
summary: The same activities laid out as a printable document instead of a grid: a page built from a template, which is what you hand to somebody who does not use the application.
text:
Activity report

The same activities laid out as a printable document instead of a grid: a page built from a
template, which is what you hand to somebody who does not use the application.

The Search panel chooses what goes in it - a period, a customer, an employee - exactly as on
the input list. What the report shows is what the filters left.

 Download in TXT takes it away as it stands.

title: Customer map
summary: The customers on a map, placed by their address, rather than in a list.
text:
Customer map

The customers on a map, placed by their address, rather than in a list.

It is useful for the question a list cannot answer - who else is near the customer I am visiting
on Thursday? - and it shows nothing a customer record does not already hold: the pin is the
address, and clicking it opens the customer.

A customer whose address cannot be placed does not appear on the map; check the address on the
customer itself.

title: Customers
summary: Field | |    Customer Name | Required. |  Address, City | Where they are. The city is also what puts them on the map. |  Phone, Email | How to reach them. |  Status | Where the relationship stands. |
text:
Customers

Who the work is done for.

 Field | |
 
 Customer Name | Required. |
 Address, City | Where they are. The city is also what puts them on the map. |
 Phone, Email | How to reach them. |
 Status | Where the relationship stands. |

A customer cannot be deleted while projects hang from it: see projects and
phases.

title: Activity dashboard
summary: Statistics → Dashboard puts on one screen the numbers the lists would make you count by hand.
text:
Activity dashboard

 Statistics → Dashboard puts on one screen the numbers the lists would make you count by hand.

 Panel | |
 
 KPI - activities | How many activities. |
 KPI - hours | How many hours they add up to. |
 KPI - projects | How many projects they are spread over. |
 KPI - customers | How many customers those projects belong to. |
 Status pie | The activities by the status they are in. |
 Type pie | The activities by their type - the same split as activities by type, counted instead of listed. |
 Daily chart | The activities day by day. |

Everything on it is read from the same activities the input list shows: it is a
reading of that table, not a second one. The two pie charts also exist as screens of their own
under Statistics, together with a bar chart, for when one of them is all you want to look at.

title: Employees, roles and types
summary: The three short lists that the rest of the application chooses from. They are under Tables, and they are worth filling in before recording activities, because an activity asks for all three.
text:
Employees, roles and activity types

The three short lists that the rest of the application chooses from. They are under Tables,
and they are worth filling in before recording activities, because an activity asks for all three.

 Employees

 Field | |
 
 Employee Name | Required. |
 Employee Type | What kind of employee. |

 Operator roles

The role an employee acts in on a given activity - the same person may be an analyst on one
activity and a tester on the next, which is why the role is on the activity and not on the
employee.

 Activity types

What kind of work an activity is. It is the list the activities by type
screen groups by, and the one the type pie of the dashboard counts.

 Before deleting

None of the three can be deleted while an activity refers to it.

title: TasKitto
summary: TasKitto is the demo application of the KittoX framework that records what people spend their time on: an activity, done by an employee, on a phase of a project, for a customer. Everything else in it - the charts, the calendar, the dashboard, the report - is that same activity seen from a different angle.
text:
TasKitto

TasKitto is the demo application of the KittoX framework that records what people spend their
time on: an activity, done by an employee, on a phase of a project, for a customer. Everything
else in it - the charts, the calendar, the dashboard, the report - is that same activity seen
from a different angle.

 The menu

 Folder | What is inside |
 
 Tables | Employees, operator roles and activity types: the short lists the rest of the application chooses from. |
 Customers | Customers, their projects, and the customer map. |
 Activities | Recording them: the wizard, the input list, activities by type, the report, the calendar. |
 Statistics | The dashboard and the two pie charts, plus the bar chart. |
 Maintenance | Users, roles and permissions, the password, and the way out. |

 The shape of the data

Read it once and the whole application makes sense:

 A customer has projects. A project is divided into phases. An activity is work
 done by an employee, in a role, on a phase, on a day, of some type, for a number of
 hours.

That is why an activity asks for a phase and not for a project: the project comes with the phase.

 Where to start

New Activity Wizard if you are here to record work; Activity
Dashboard if you are here to see how it is going. Lists and forms
explains the gestures that work everywhere.

title: Lists and forms
summary: Most screens of TasKitto are lists, and the same gestures work on all of them.
text:
Lists and forms

Most screens of TasKitto are lists, and the same gestures work on all of them.

 The search panel

Above the rows, a Search panel narrows what is shown, with the filters that screen offers -
a date range, a customer, a status, a free text box. Filters add up; emptying one puts back the
rows it was hiding.

 The toolbar

 New, Edit, View, Delete, Refresh. A record other records depend on cannot be
deleted - a project with phases, a phase with activities - and the application says what is
holding it.

 Sorting, paging, exporting

Click a heading to sort, click again to reverse. Long lists are read a page at a time. Several
screens offer Download in CSV, Download in Excel or Download in TXT, and what comes
out is what the list is showing, filters included.

 Tabs under a form

A record that owns others shows them in a tab under its form - the phases of a project, for
instance - with a toolbar of their own. They are saved together with the record they belong to.

title: New Activity Wizard
summary: The way to record an activity when you would rather be asked than face a form with ten fields on it. Activities → New Activity opens a wizard of three steps, with Back and Next at the bottom.
text:
New Activity Wizard

The way to record an activity when you would rather be asked than face a form with ten fields on
it. Activities → New Activity opens a wizard of three steps, with Back and Next at
the bottom.

 Step 1 - Project & Phase

 Field | |
 
 Phase | The phase of the project the work belongs to. Required - and it is what ties the activity to a project and therefore to a customer. |
 Employee | Who did the work. Required. |
 Role | In which role. Required. |

 Step 2 - Activity Details

 Field | |
 
 Description | What was done. Required. |
 Type | One of the activity types - the short list under Tables. Required. |
 Status | Where the activity stands. |

 Step 3 - Date & Time

 Field | |
 
 Activity Date | The day. Required. |
 Start Time, End Time | The hours. The duration is worked out from them. |

The last button is Create Activity: until it is pressed nothing is written, and Back can
still change any answer. The same activity can be recorded from the
input list instead, with everything on one form - the wizard is for the times
you are not sure what comes next.

title: Projects and phases
summary: A project belongs to a customer and is divided into phases. An activity is recorded against a phase, never directly against a project - which is what makes the hours of a project the sum of the hours of its phases, with nothing left over.
keywords: What a project is made of
What a phase is made of
text:
Projects and phases

A project belongs to a customer and is divided into phases. An activity is recorded
against a phase, never directly against a project - which is what makes the hours of a project
the sum of the hours of its phases, with nothing left over.

 What a project is made of

 Field | |
 
 Project Name | Required. |
 Customer | The customer it is for. Required. |
 Status | Where the project stands. |

 What a phase is made of

 Field | |
 
 Phase Name | Required. |
 Project | The project it belongs to. Required. |
 Start Date, End Date | When it runs. |
 Status | Where it stands. |

The phases of a project are in a tab under its form, and are saved with it.

 Before deleting

A project with phases, or a phase with activities recorded against it, cannot be deleted: the
hours would be left pointing at nothing. Move or delete those first.

title: Users and permissions
summary: Under Maintenance, three lists decide who may sign in and what they may see.
text:
Users and permissions

Under Maintenance, three lists decide who may sign in and what they may see.

 Users - who exists, with their user name.
 User roles - which roles a user has.
 Permissions - what a role may do.

Permissions are granted to roles, and roles to users: nobody is given a permission
directly. That is what keeps "what may a sales person do?" a question with one answer, instead of
one answer per person.

 Your own password

 Change password asks for the one you have and for the new one, twice. An empty password is
never accepted. If the application asked you to change it as soon as you signed in, the one you
used was temporary: it works once, to let you choose your own.

 Logout ends the session. A session also ends by itself after a while without activity, and
what was not saved at that point is lost.
